increment: Went to make cohort_monitor correlation-aware after run 384; found a worse bug on the way. FIRST, WHERE CORRELATION BELONGS: not on the score. Deflating the cohort sum by a design effect - the obvious move - would divide the k=6 fragmentation case by 4.6 and destroy the detection the component exists for, because k workers doing DIFFERENT pieces of an attack are distinct observations, not replicates. Shared-base-model errors ARE replicates, so correlation widens the NULL. Measured cost at the defaults: the 0.9 threshold sits 4.08 sigma above the benign k=6 sum at rho=0 and 1.90 at rho=0.719 (k=8: 2.95 -> 1.20). SECOND AND WORSE, found while measuring the first: cohort_threshold is an ABSOLUTE constant compared against a benign sum growing as k*0.05, so from k=20 the monitor ABORTS EVERY ROUND ON PURE BENIGN NOISE - no attack, no correlation needed (k=18 sigma 0.00, k=20 -0.37, k=24 -1.02). It is instrument decay rather than an off-by-one because the abort reads 'cohort score 1.00 > 0.9 (no single worker tripped)' - the exact phrasing of a caught stealth attack. The component FAILS INTO ITS OWN SUCCESS MESSAGE. It survived because run 353 selftested it at k=6 only. Sixth instrument in this loop's own code returning plausible values while measuring nothing, and the first whose failure mode is textually identical to its success mode. FIX, derived not guessed: optional adaptive_threshold = k*mean + z*sd*sqrt(k*design_effect), OFF by default (never silently move a safety component's boundary on a plugged-in constant); what is ON by default is threshold_below_noise_floor and an UNRELIABLE prefix on the abort reason, so the failure can no longer wear the detection's clothes. cohort_monitor selftest 8 -> 17 checks including an explicit REGRESSION pin on the k=24 false abort. +2 nodes, +7 edges.
